\[
P(i, j) = \frac{\#\{p : q(p) = i,\ q(p + d) = j\}}{\#\{p\}},
\qquad
\text{contrast} = \sum_{i,j} P(i, j)\, (i - j)^2,
\qquad
\text{energy} = \sqrt{\sum_{i,j} P(i, j)^2}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(q\): The quantized luma
- \(d\): The offset of the pair
- \(P\): The normalized co-occurrence matrix

The luma is quantized to q, from 0 to levels - 1. For an offset d, the gray-level co-occurrence matrix P counts how often level i has level j at the offset d. It is divided by the number of pairs. Symmetric counting adds each pair both ways. Each property sums P with a weight. Contrast weights the squared difference of levels, so it is high on rough texture. Dissimilarity uses the absolute difference. Homogeneity weights 1 / (1 + (i - j)^2), high where neighbors match. The angular second moment sums P^2, and energy is its square root, high where few pairs dominate. Correlation measures how linearly neighboring levels depend on each other. Entropy is high where many pairs are equally common. All follow scikit-image's graycoprops. The map computes P of the window around each pixel, counting the pairs with both pixels inside it, and stretches the property to the full gray range.
